advances: A finite-dimensional theorem about choosing one common probability vector before the body direction and the circuit selection. The gap is a dual-norm quantity in the chosen direction space.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
For fixed $\pi$ and $v$, nonnegative weights and independent menu choices give $\sum_p\pi_p\min_{g\in\Gamma_p}g(v)=\min_{g_p\in\Gamma_p}(\sum_p\pi_pg_p)(v)$. The two minima, over $v$ in the unit ball and over the product of menus, commute. A covector's minimum on the signed unit ball is the negative of its dual norm. Maximizing in $\pi$ gives $V_{\mathrm{fixed}}=-R$. All displayed extrema exist because the domains are compact and the functions continuous, including the extremal values as functions of $\pi$ by uniform continuity on the compact products.

An optimizing $\pi$ gives $R=0$ exactly when its weighted Minkowski sum is $\{0\}$. Holding all choices except at one $p$ fixed and subtracting shows that any menu with $\pi_p>0$ is a singleton. Its selected covectors must balance, which is also sufficient. For a given $\pi$, varying just the $p$th menu shows its weighted sum has diameter at least $\pi_pD_p$, and its largest norm is at least half that diameter. Thus its largest norm is at least $\tfrac12\max_p\pi_pD_p\ge(2\sum_pD_p^{-1})^{-1}$, the last inequality following by summing $\pi_p\le(\max_q\pi_qD_q)/D_p$.

In the rank-one example $\Gamma_0=[a-r,a+r]$, $\Gamma_1=[-a-r,-a+r]$, $a>r>0$, every selection has opposite signs and hence a positive convex balance. Directionwise protection has value $\max_p\min_{g\in\Gamma_p}gv=(a-r)|v|$. At weight $t$ on the first menu, the weighted sum is an interval of center $a(2t-1)$ and radius $r$, so its largest absolute value is $|a(2t-1)|+r$. The best frozen weight is $t=1/2$, giving $R=r$.

For directions in a cone $D$, the claimed guarantee is precisely the test defining membership of each weighted sum in $D^+$. A cone can admit a nonsingleton weighted sum, for example one menu $[1,2]$ on the direction cone $[0,\infty)\subset\mathbb R$. In the signed case $D=E$ one has $D^+=\{0\}$ and the singleton argument applies.

statement:
Let $I$ be finite nonempty and $\Gamma_p$ be nonempty compact convex subsets of the dual of a finite-dimensional normed space $E$. Put
$$
R=\min_{\pi\in\Delta_I}\max_{g_p\in\Gamma_p}\Bigl\|\sum_p\pi_p g_p\Bigr\|_*,
\qquad
V_{\mathrm{fixed}}=\max_{\pi\in\Delta_I}\min_{\|v\|\le1}\sum_p\pi_p\min_{g\in\Gamma_p}g(v).
$$
Then both extrema are attained and $V_{\mathrm{fixed}}=-R$. Moreover $R=0$ exactly when some $\pi\in\Delta_I$ is supported on singleton menus $\Gamma_p=\{a_p\}$ satisfying $\sum_p\pi_pa_p=0$. If every dual-norm diameter $D_p$ of $\Gamma_p$ is positive, then
$$
R\ge\frac{1}{2\sum_p D_p^{-1}}>0.
$$
For a one-sided admissible cone $D\subset E$, a fixed $\pi$ guarantees a nonnegative response for every $v\in D$ and every selection exactly when $\sum_p\pi_p\Gamma_p\subseteq D^+$, where $D^+=\{g:g(v)\ge0\ \forall v\in D\}$.
title: The frozen circuit game has an exact dual-norm gap
